proposals.evidence: DEDR5052 explicitly gives Kolami mūndiŋ three things, alongside muggur three men and muyal three women. LSI mūŋdīŋ Three fits the nonhuman numeral; its written ŋ before d and long ī differ from DEDR n/i and are retained as source-transcription qualifications, not corrected.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4411 explicitly includes Kolami pedda a male and Naiki pedda man, male within the great/big family. LSI peddā Man matches this branch apart from final vowel quantity. The article-level target does not require the reflex to mean great or match its displayed head.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1711(b) explicitly gives Kolami gurram horse, beside Telugu guṟṟamu and Naiki ghurram. LSI gurrām Horse / Horse (male) differs in final-vowel quantity. The article questions a possible Indo-Aryan origin for the Telugu form; this family proposal preserves that contact uncertainty and does not assert a specific borrowing route.
